label: ports-w2h-n1
_why: PORT-SUBSIDY APPROACH 1 (user-directed 2026-08-16): does wants_to_have on ALL FIVE port tier keys end the colonial ACCESS FAMINE that the full mandate removal produced? vancost-nosub-n2 measured GBR/FRA overseas states at 0.50-0.78 market access for five decades (1840-1890) because unsubsidised sail/steam/industrial ports run at ~1% staffing (convoy famine), self-healing only when the e3 modern port - the first self-sustaining rung (0.85-0.94 staffed unsubsidised) - scales in the 1890s. wants_to_have = subsidise-if-affordable: the majors' early port bills are small, so the mandate-free affordability gate should staff them; the question is whether it fires at all (nice_to_have never fired for majors) and at what bill. RAILWAYS AND POWER STAY nice_to_have by explicit instruction - no mandate even on early railways. DECISION RULE (self-judged): SOLVED if no overseas state of the six tag countries sits below 0.9 access for 2+ consecutive dumps in 1840-1890 AND the world port-subsidy bill stays sane (well under the old full mandate's 374-455k/wk; vanilla's own trio mandate ran ~75k/wk); FAILED if the 0.5-plateau famine reappears - then approach 2 (conditional early-port mandate via possible-gated strategy variants) runs as the next n=1.
_arms: ports_w2h = {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.ports_w2h.json} - NOT committed (gitignored). Regenerate: the vancost_nosub recipe (flat 1.0x vanilla-anchor building_cost, see schedules/vancost_nosub_n2.json _arms) with building_subsidies = trade_center:vanilla + 5 port tier keys wants_to_have + 4 railway keys nice_to_have + 3 power keys nice_to_have. Then cp config/tech_tree_options.json config/tech_tree_options.ports_w2h.json.
_comparison: vancost-nosub-n2 (20260816_011552) = the no-mandate baseline with the famine; flatcost-n1/vanilla n=4 for subsidy-bill scale. Same 1.0x cost book as the n=2 so access/staffing/GDP read against it directly.
_cost: 1 run x 64 in-game years, ~60-75 min wall.
